content.text: Hello! Today, we will learn about the **Diameter** of a Binary Tree. The diameter is the length of the longest path between any two nodes in the tree. This path may or may not pass through the root node. Let's see how to find it!

The diameter of a tree is the longest path between any two leaf nodes. For any node, the longest path passing through that node is the sum of the heights of its left and right subtrees:
**Path passing through node = (Left Height + 1) + (Right Height + 1)** (if height of empty subtree is -1).
Thus, the diameter of the tree is the maximum path sum found at any node in the tree!

content.text: Let's summarize: The diameter of a tree is the longest distance between any two nodes. We compute it recursively in $O(N)$ time by updating a running maximum of $(\text{leftHeight} + \text{rightHeight} + 2)$ during our height calculations.
